new_findings_today.title: Shell grep produced a false-positive match for the atlas static-coordinate string on UTF-8 Hindi HTML
new_findings_today.detail: An initial `grep -l "23.5"` pass over the 10 saved Hindi destination-page HTML snapshots reported 10/10 matches, including vishnuprayag — which is a Leaflet-template page that does not render the Atlas component at all and should not match. Re-checking with Python's UTF-8-aware string search (`"23.5" in text`) found the true result: 9/10, with vishnuprayag correctly absent. The shell grep's byte-level matching against multi-byte Devanagari UTF-8 sequences produced a spurious hit. This is a QA-harness methodology note, not a site defect — the site behavior is internally consistent (atlas bug only appears on atlas-template pages, in either locale).
new_findings_today.evidence: qa/findings/2026-07-13/html/hi_vishnuprayag.html: shell `grep -c "23.5"` returns 1, but `LC_ALL=C grep -ao` and a direct Python `text.find("23.5")` both find no real match (idx=-1); Python confirms 0 atlas-viewBox and 14 'leaflet' string occurrences in that file, consistent with it being Leaflet-template.
new_findings_today.recommendation: For future runs: verify any grep-based text match against Hindi/Devanagari HTML with a UTF-8-aware tool (Python, or `grep` with explicit `--text` and a known-good locale) before reporting it, especially for short numeric-looking patterns like '23.5' that are more likely to collide with multi-byte sequences by chance.
